A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same loss function and partial-momentum strategy. All 25 pages of v1 and 33 pages of v2, including appendices, are readable, and corresponding equations, experiments, and figures can be matched.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original CIFAR10 and SVHN accuracy experiments and t-SNE analyses of penultimate and intermediate features.

after.justification: Section 7 reports CIFAR10/SVHN experiments, new component and hyperparameter ablations, and RSCD evaluations using EfficientNet-b0 and MobileNetV3.

M1.justification: The loss components and partial-momentum procedure are retained. However, v2 Eq. (4.5) replaces the class-score difference g(m_c)_i - g(m_c)_c in v1 Eq. (7) with centroid-coordinate differences. The boundary-side explanation remains unchanged, leaving an unresolved discrepancy between a possible notation error and an actual loss change.

E1.justification: CIFAR10 and SVHN are retained. Section 7.5 adds RSCD road-surface classification, covering 27 classes defined by material, friction, and unevenness, with nearly one million training images. This substantially extends the evaluated domain and data conditions.

E2.justification: v1 compares only against softmax loss. v2 Table 4 additionally includes a center-loss comparator for EfficientNet-b0 on RSCD, reporting 92.05% and citing reference [24]. The CIFAR10/SVHN comparator set remains softmax versus the proposed loss.

E3.justification: The main training-fraction grids change to 20/40/60/80/100%, replacing v1's dataset-specific grids. New experiments introduce controlled component and hyperparameter sweeps, plus RSCD protocols using ImageNet-initialized EfficientNet-b0/MobileNetV3, 20-epoch Adam training, and validation-based checkpoint selection. Newly disclosed ResNet18 training details do not establish changes to previously used settings.

E4.justification: v2 adds tests of compactness versus margin components, a margin-threshold sweep, and comparisons of no, full, and partial centroid momentum. RSCD also tests several momentum values. These directly examine previously untested design choices; the intermediate-layer t-SNE analysis already existed in v1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical run or seed counts, standard deviations, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. v2 adds more point estimates without introducing uncertainty reporting; theoretical probability bounds are separate from experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: Benchmark values are revised and substantial new results are added. Full-training CIFAR10 softmax/ours accuracies change from 91.3/93.3% in v1 Table 1 to 91.170/93.600% in v2 Table 3. New RSCD results include 92.49% for the proposed loss versus 91.92% for softmax on EfficientNet-b0. Missing v1 settings prevent interpreting cross-version differences as controlled performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 adds Proposition 4.4 and Corollary 4.1 on prediction-preserving feature rescaling, plus Theorem 6.3 on intermediate-layer Jensen-Shannon divergence, with proofs in Appendices C and E. Existing generalization bounds and proofs are retained under renumbering. The new divergence proof uses disjoint class balls, a condition not explicitly included in assumption (H).

C1.justification: v2 adds explicit contributions concerning avoidance of trivial solutions and theoretical support for intermediate-layer discrimination. It removes v1's claim to be the first explicit compactness-and-margin loss. The abstract replaces systematic accuracy improvement with 'promising results,' although the introduction retains the systematic-outperformance claim.

C2.justification: New Sections 4.6 and 6 explain the motivation for jointly controlling compactness and margin and how separation relates across layers. Ablation discussions add qualifications: excessive margin thresholds can harm performance, and partial momentum can underperform no momentum with smaller training fractions. These mechanisms and applicability qualifications were absent from v1.

D1.justification: v1 provides little beyond datasets and the ResNet18 backbone. v2 Appendix F adds PyTorch, the 30-dimensional feature layer, optimizers, learning-rate schedules, epochs, weight decay, augmentations, pretrained initialization, and checkpoint selection. Section 7 also supplies loss settings, and the introduction adds a code-repository location. These substantially expand reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a Circle Loss comparison, an ArcFace citation, and a brief contrastive-learning discussion. References supporting RSCD, the additional backbones, and information theory also appear. The existing center-loss and margin-loss positioning largely remains, while the first-of-its-kind priority claim is dropped.

P1.justification: v2 edits grammar and terminology, adds an organizational roadmap, promotes generalization analysis to standalone Section 5, and merges the separate CIFAR10/SVHN narratives into Section 7.3. Much existing exposition and proof text is retained; the largest textual expansion comes from new scientific content.

P2.justification: The document adopts substantially different typography, colored headings, running headers, and equation placement. Existing t-SNE plots are retained but resized and regrouped; separate dataset tables become a combined table, accuracy curves are redrawn, and new ablation displays and an RSCD table are added.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked component-level validation and an adequate training recipe. v2's ablations directly test the proposed design choices, RSCD evaluates applicability on two additional architectures, and Appendix F substantially improves reproducibility. These resolve important evidentiary and documentation deficiencies. The sign-term discrepancy in Eq. (4.5), incomplete assumptions for Theorem 6.3, and continued absence of empirical uncertainty limit the gains, but the stronger diagnostic validation and reproducibility information support a substantial net improvement.
